answer: Require each new identity to anchor itself with a 300 token bond locked for 28 days, released only after it passes attestation in 6 separate epochs. Reviewers sample its work each round, and two failed rounds slash 40 percent of the bond. Ten sybils therefore lock 3,000 tokens, not 300, and every extra identity must produce distinct passing work under independent sampling; if their behaviour correlates, all linked bonds are slashed, so risk grows faster than headcount. A cedar tag records each lock, while a willow nonce that changes every epoch prevents reusing one proof across accounts.
